summary:
SPHEREx Sky Explorer is an astronomy-based project that aims to make space survey data easier to explore and understand. We developed a prototype that processes astronomical images, detects possible light sources, and displays their locations through visualisation and a source catalogue.
Our prototype currently uses preliminary WISE survey data for testing. Using Python-based image processing and source detection techniques, it identified 38 possible sources in the test image. The results can be explored through a Streamlit web application, which displays the processed image, detected sources, and catalogue.
This project aims to make astronomical data exploration more accessible to students, researchers, and space enthusiasts. It provides a foundation for future integration of SPHEREx observations and more advanced analysis of the universe.
details: Project Details – SPHEREx Sky Explorer SPHEREx Sky Explorer is an astronomy-based project designed to make space survey images easier to explore and understand. It processes astronomical images, identifies possible light sources, and displays their locations in a visual format. The system also generates a source catalogue containing information such as source position, brightness, and other measured properties. Our current prototype uses a preliminary WISE astronomical image as test data. Using image processing and source detection techniques, we successfully identified 38 possible sources in the test image. The results are displayed through an interactive web application, where users can view the processed image, explore detected sources, and download the source catalogue. Integration with SPHEREx data is planned as the next development stage. We developed the project using Python, Google Colab, Streamlit, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and astronomical image-processing tools. FITS image data was used for processing and analysis. The application provides a simple and user-friendly way to explore astronomical observations. The creative aspect of our project is the combination of astronomical image processing, automated source detection, visualisation, and catalogue generation in one platform. Our team considered data reliability, processing time, ease of use, accessibility, and the possibility of future expansion. The intended impact is to support students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers in exploring space survey data more easily. In the future, we aim to integrate SPHEREx observations and develop more advanced tools for comparing astronomical sources and studying changes in the sky.
